questions.prompt: Business Intelligence is best described as:
options: Technologies + processes that transform raw data into meaningful information for better business decisions
questions.explain: BI = the **data → information → decision** pipeline: gathering, storing (warehouse), analyzing and presenting business data so decisions are evidence-based rather than gut-based.

questions.prompt: Order the standard BI architecture data flow:
items: Front-end: reporting, dashboards, OLAP, data mining
questions.explain: **Sources → ETL → warehouse/marts → front-end analytics.** Every Ch2 exam question hangs off this picture — know which component does what and in which order data moves.

questions.prompt: The TRANSFORM step of ETL includes:
options: Cleansing, standardizing formats, deduplicating, deriving fields, integrating sources
questions.explain: Extract = pull from sources; **Transform = clean/standardize/derive/integrate** (the heavy lifting — exactly what Alteryx does in Lab 1); Load = write into the warehouse.

questions.prompt: Data warehouse vs operational (OLTP) database — which contrast is correct?
options: Warehouse: subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile for ANALYSIS · OLTP: current, volatile, optimized for fast transactions
Warehouse handles daily transactions; OLTP stores history
questions.explain: Inmon's four warehouse words: **subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile** — built for queries/analysis over history. OLTP serves the day-to-day inserts/updates of operations.

questions.prompt: Which list contains BI FRONT-END applications?
options: Reports, dashboards, OLAP analysis, data mining / predictive tools
questions.explain: The front-end is what decision-makers touch: **reporting, dashboards/scorecards, OLAP (slice/dice/drill), data mining & predictive analytics** — Tableau and the Alteryx predictive palette are this course's instances.

questions.prompt: Dashboard vs report — the practical difference:
options: Dashboard = at-a-glance visual monitor of multiple KPIs, often interactive; report = structured, detailed, typically static/printable
questions.explain: **Dashboard** = single screen, many KPIs, interactivity (filters/drill). **Report** = depth + structure for one topic (the Alteryx Render-to-PDF output in Challenge S1.8 is a report).

questions.prompt: The main business value of BI is:
options: Faster, evidence-based decisions — spotting trends, problems and opportunities in data instead of intuition
questions.explain: Quote-worthy line: BI turns data into **actionable insight** — better/faster decisions, competitive advantage, performance monitoring. Tie any open answer back to DECISIONS.

options: A subject/department-focused subset of the warehouse (e.g., just sales)
A backup of the OLTP database
questions.explain: **Mart = departmental slice of the warehouse** — smaller scope, faster queries for one business area. Architecture diagrams place marts between the warehouse and the front-end.
